name: Inferior colliculus
summary: The lower pair of tectal bumps and the obligatory relay of the ascending auditory pathway: every lateral lemniscus fiber ends here before the signal goes on through the brachium of the inferior colliculus to the medial geniculate body and the auditory cortex. Its central nucleus is tonotopically organized, and it also mediates auditory startle and the reflex turning of eyes and head toward a sound through connections with the superior colliculus.

anatomy.location: Dorsal caudal midbrain below the superior colliculi and above the trochlear nerve exit, on either side of the midline, with the brachium running rostrolaterally to the medial geniculate body.

function: Frequency analysis, sound localization and the integration of monaural and binaural pathways; relay to the thalamus and reflex orientation to sound.

bestView.label: caudal tectal plate at the trochlear level
inferior colliculus below the superior colliculus

imaging.normalAppearance: Lower of the two tectal bumps on sagittal images; on axial slices at the inferior colliculus level the aqueduct lies just in front. Hypoxic or Wernicke lesions can produce symmetrical T2 hyperintensity here.

pathology.finding: Symmetrical FLAIR hyperintensity of the inferior colliculi with the periaqueductal gray and medial thalami.
Expansion of the caudal tectum with aqueductal compression.

lesionEffects.deficit: Impaired sound localization and central hearing disturbance without deafness

examination: Hearing thresholds (normal) versus localization of sound with eyes closed
pearls: Central auditory lesions above the cochlear nuclei do not cause deafness in one ear
Bilateral bright inferior colliculi on FLAIR in a malnourished or alcohol-dependent patient: give thiamine
